drivingQuestion: What does the mishna mean by alal — the nuchal ligament, or the meat residue left on the hide by the knife?
outcomeNote: The two definitions are laid down side by side and not adjudicated here; they are tested against sources in the unit that follows.

segments.he: וְהָאָלָל. מַאי אָלָל? רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: מַרְטְקָא, וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: בָּשָׂר שֶׁפְּלָטַתּוּ סַכִּין.
segments.en: §The mishna teaches that «the alal» joins together with the flesh to constitute the requisite egg-bulk to impart the impurity of food, despite not being considered food itself. The Gemara asks: To «what» is the term «alal» referring? «Rabbi Yoḥanan says:» It is referring to «the nuchal ligament [marteka]. And Reish Lakish says:» It is referring to the «meat» residue «that» is attached to the hide after «the knife has flayed» the flesh.
